items.publisher: European Journal of Business Economics & Management
items.venue: European Journal of Business Economics & Management
items.summary: Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) modeling remains a cornerstone of corporate valuation, yet its practical reliability hinges critically on the accuracy and stability of key input parameters—particularly the discount rate, terminal growth rate, and forecast horizon—and on the model’s resilience to parameter perturbations.
items.finding: Robustness testing demonstrates that models calibrated using rolling five-year beta windows and dynamic terminal multiples exhibit 61% higher stability under market shifts than static single-period benchmarks.

items.title: Value investing in emerging markets: The effectiveness of the Piotroski F-score strategy in Poland as a Central and Eastern European case study
items.summary: The aim of this article is to verify the investment effectiveness of a long-only strategy based on the Piotroski F-score indicator on the Polish equity market, relative to the passive ‘buy and hold’ strategy tracking the broad WIG index.
